result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **HubSpot or Pipedrive**\. The best choice depends on whether you want an all-round customer management system or a CRM focused on winning sales.

You don't need an expensive, complicated CRM when you have a team of 3–10 people. You need something everyone will actually use, that keeps track of leads, customers, conversations and follow-ups.

search_results.description: TechRadar’s 2026 guide reviews CRM platforms for small businesses, emphasizing that modern systems combine contact and pipeline management with AI, lead generation, automation, billing, and post-sale operations. Salesforce is the overall recommendation, offering scalable sales, service, marketing, Slack integration, and autonomous Agentforce workflows; its Starter plan begins at $25 per user monthly, while advanced automation requires the $100 Pro plan. Freshsales is highlighted for value, with affordable plans, Freddy AI, sentiment analysis, email synchronization, and new lead-capture tools. Zoho CRM is the easiest to adopt, combining intuitive workflows, lead generation, reporting, and integration with the wider Zoho ecosystem. Other recommendations include HubSpot for its capable free plan, Monday Sales CRM for sales teams, Streak for Gmail users, Pipedrive for user experience, Insightly for project management, and Workbooks for reporting and financial tracking. The guide advises comparing usability, scalability, integrations, automation, support, and total AI costs, since providers use different billing models. Effective adoption also requires clear objectives, training, ongoing support, and employee feedback.

search_results.title: Pipedrive CRM: Hands-on testing - I can't believe how easy it is to navigate
search_results.description: TechRadar Pro's hands-on review finds Pipedrive CRM an intuitive, sales-focused platform particularly well suited to small and midsize businesses. Its standout feature is a visual, drag-and-drop sales pipeline that simplifies deal tracking, while customizable contact management, multiple pipelines, forecasting, visual reporting, and workflow automation help teams improve productivity. Recent AI enhancements, including Pulse, provide deal prioritization, win-probability scores, activity scheduling, and context-aware email drafting. Pipedrive also offers mobile apps, over 400 third-party integrations, an open API, and project management features that streamline the transition from closing deals to customer onboarding. Usability is excellent, supported by extensive learning resources and generally responsive customer service, although advanced automations can require additional setup and support quality varies. Pricing starts at $14 per user monthly for Lite, rising to $39 for Growth, $59 for Premium, and $79 for Ultimate, with annual billing offering savings of up to 17%. A 14-day free trial is available, but there is no permanent free plan. Additional features, including lead generation and email marketing, cost extra. The main drawbacks are limited native marketing automation, potentially expensive add-ons, and entry-level restrictions. Overall, Pipedrive is an excellent choice for sales-first teams prioritizing simplicity, efficiency, and pipeline visibility over comprehensive business management.
